sources.finding: Hybrid: state in retained entities, a view's render builds an element tree each frame; layout by Taffy; custom elements for large lists and editors.

A small fixed primitive set: rectangles by SDF, shadows, glyphs, icons, images. Shaped text cached per text and font. Alpha-only glyph atlas with up to 16 subpixel variants. Icons are CPU-rastered alpha masks. Layers and stacking contexts give z-order.

A persistent widget tree with central focus, pointer and AccessKit handling, and a test harness on the tree; user-facing paradigm is built on top. Its renderer is wgpu, so architecture only, no reuse.
Retained Control tree, one focused control, event routing with accept_event and mouse_filter, cascading theme, accessibility_name on nodes.
Godot added screen reader support to Control nodes through AccessKit; editor coverage incomplete, classified experimental by press. A pro-class editor UI retrofitted AccessKit onto a retained tree.
Editor docks: fixed dock slots, layout_key, saved per-dock layout, positions remembered. Same shape as STU-SHL-063 regions.
IDs are hashed from the widget path; keeps minimal retained data; FAQ never mentions accessibility; docking in a branch; IME needs the HWND on the main viewport.

The Vulkan backend takes Instance, PhysicalDevice, Device, Queue from the host and never creates a device, window or surface; it owns its pipeline, font atlas and texture descriptors; supports dynamic rendering. This is the O4 renderer contract.

IME off by default; set_ime_allowed, set_ime_cursor_area; set_ime_purpose has no effect on Windows; set_cursor_visible hides only within the window on Windows; focus_window steals focus and must only be used when expected.
with_active and with_visible exist; no Windows note on with_active.
Current 0.25.2 has set_author_id and numeric setters, no custom-property API. Locked 0.21.1 has them too (REG lib.rs:1755,1804).
0.15.1. Flexbox, Grid, Block. Low-level API for embedding with own storage; all dependencies optional. GPUI pins Taffy.
Allocator takes host instance, device, physical_device; latest 0.28.0, lock pins 0.27.0.
Shelf atlas with deallocation. Rejected, see text position.
Gamma correction thins small glyphs; stem darkening only with linear blending and gamma correction, otherwise heavy and fuzzy.

positions.blocker: O4: boundary between the shell's UI layer and Kumihimo's renderer
positions.decision: Three layers, owner per concern. (A) Controls and UI model, toolkit-free, Kumihimo-owned: widget semantics, widget drawing as a display list, layout inside panels, focus order, gesture arbitration, text-edit state including IME preedit and caret, semantic tree. (B) Vulkan renderer, Kumihimo-owned: display list to Vulkan commands on a host-supplied instance, device, queue and target; owns its pipeline, glyph atlas and texture slots; never creates a device, window or surface. (C) Host platform layer, Handshake's shell in the product and a thin asset-local host in standalone Studio: window, event pump, surface and swapchain, device ownership, DPI source, OS IME calls, the AccessKit platform adapter, pop-out windows, recovery. Text: shaping and rasterisation stay in hsk-studio-type behind a text port defined by (A), atlas in (B), so Kumihimo never depends on a Studio crate. IME: OS binding in (C), composition state in (A). AccessKit: node production in (A), platform adapter in (C). Widget drawing: (A) decides, (B) executes.
positions.why: It gives each concern one owner and matches the only field-proven split for a toolkit that must live inside someone else's Vulkan device: Dear ImGui's Vulkan backend receives device and queue and creates neither window nor device. GUI-DESKTOP-025 and GUI-DESKTOP-037 require that a window not be its own GPU authority, so (B) cannot own a device. STU-ARC-023 makes Kumihimo the renderer owner, HANDOFF blocker 3 makes Handshake the owner of window, focus, IME, DPI: this split honours both and resolves their overlap on text, IME and AccessKit, which neither record settled.
positions.risk: Handshake's future shell might want its own text or control drawing, which would duplicate (A); WP-KERNEL-012 stays on eframe (O1) and cannot host (B).
positions.control: (C) is a small named port set: device grant, target image, input event stream, IME commands, semantic-tree sink. Standalone host implements it now and proves the port is enough. O1 is untouched and does not gate Studio. A CPU painter of the same display list keeps a last-resort embed path (image in any host), UNVERIFIED for that use.
positions.proven_wrong_if: A port change is needed in (B) to implement IME, resize, device loss or pop-out; or (A) has to import winit, ash or accesskit platform types; or the display list cannot express a surface the 25 panels need without a host callback.
positions.unblocks: O5, O6, every lane below; gives MT-197 and MT-203 owners a concrete client shape.

positions.blocker: O5: where the control mechanic lives
positions.decision: D8 stands: Kumihimo is the owner. Physical sequence: the mechanic stays in hsk-studio-controls and the new UI crates are born in the Studio workspace, with a mechanical rule that they depend on no Studio engine crate. At a named gate (spine gate passed, or before any Handshake adoption, whichever comes first) one lift lane moves them to Kumihimo/product beside kumihimo-egui, renames them kumihimo-*, updates assets-index.yaml, and Studio consumes the lifted tree by exact tree hash. What stays in Studio after the lift: Studio's descriptor tables, report.rs (Observe frames), harness-core panel routes, panel view functions. RF-05 starts now in hsk-studio-controls and does not wait.
positions.why: STU-ARC-023 calls Kumihimo owner, yet kumihimo-core has no control kinds; ControlRecord is an egui-adapter report struct with id, label, bounds, target, enabled. All working mechanic (descriptors, value legality, undo-friendly store, availability, menu audit) is in hsk-studio-controls, 2,715 lines, on another branch from Kumihimo. Moving first means every widget change lands twice: Kumihimo first, re-read, then a Studio pin bump, against an unsettled API, with a dozen parallel lanes and an Operator asking for rapid code. Nothing is forked, since no Kumihimo control mechanic exists to diverge from. Field: GPUI lives in its app's repo and co-evolves with it; toolkits are extracted once an API has met a real app.

positions.blocker: RF-02: docking, multiwindow, IME, DPI, AccessKit, truthful states; route
positions.decision: Rewrite the RF-02 target: remove egui_tiles and PopOutManager as stated means. Docking uses kumihimo-core as the arrangement model: one Core with one root workspace per region of STU-SHL-003, so a cross-region panel move is one Core command and therefore one transaction. Edge rails, seams and slots are drawn by the dock layer in (A). IME, DPI, pop-out are host (C) over winit. Empty, loading, error, denied and recovery are first-class node states in the tree. Limits: Limits::unbounded() opts in for the centre tree, the edge cap of 4 is enforced by the dock layer.
positions.why: kumihimo-core already holds frames, views, tabs, groups, nested split and grid plans, docking intents with preview and snap candidates, float and redock, persistence and restore, std-only, forbid(unsafe), with 29 owning adapter tests in its record. STU-SHL-063 wants one tree per region, which Godot's fixed dock slots also show. GUI-DESKTOP-007's no-gap rule is the Core default: GeometryContext gap 0. It is the one existing piece of D8 that truly fits.

positions.decision: Retained node arena, rebuilt per panel by a pure view function when that panel's state revision changes. Authoring reads like immediate mode; no closures hold &mut Viewer; every widget declares its action as data; nodes are keyed by author_id; scroll, caret, hover and active gesture live in a store keyed by the same id. No frame is rendered while nothing changes.
positions.why: Requirements decide this: an AccessKit tree and a model-readable state tree with stable ids (STU-MDL-002, 105, 106) that exist without a frame; set_value through the same path as a drag (STU-SHL-107); parallel headless clients; idle quiet. Field: GPUI builds elements per frame over retained entities; Masonry and Godot hold retained trees and both connect AccessKit centrally, and Godot is doing it on a pro editor. Dear ImGui is the pure-immediate benchmark and its FAQ does not mention accessibility. A view function also gives the Elm split that hosted.rs already approximates, which makes the operator path and the model path one code path.
positions.risk: Over-rebuild of large lists (layers, swatches, timeline rows); action-as-data adds an enum variant for each new control; panels with local edit buffers need explicit state.
positions.control: Virtualised list node with a row callback by index; custom canvas node for timeline. Panel-local buffers keep their existing state structs (HostedState). Dirty scope is per panel, so a timeline tick does not rebuild the Inspect Dock.
positions.proven_wrong_if: Target, on the dev box in release: rebuild, layout and display list for a 300-node Inspect Dock exceed 8 ms; or idle shows any queue submission. Both are read from gui frame stats.
positions.unblocks: Tree crate API, all panel lanes, model driving.

positions.decision: Five units with one-way deps, none of them new in engines. hsk-studio-controls (existing: descriptors, values, gesture maths, availability, menu). hsk-studio-ui (new, no unsafe, no GPU, no window: node arena and builder, widgets, Taffy layout, theme tokens from JSON, input model, focus, gesture arbiter, text-edit state, dock layer over kumihimo-core, display list, hit test, semantic tree, CPU painter). hsk-studio-ui-text (new: text port over hsk-studio-type, caches, bundled UI fonts). hsk-studio-ui-vk (new, unsafe allowed and isolated here: display list on host-supplied ash device). hsk-studio-gui-host (new binary crate: winit, accesskit_winit, swapchain, transient device, the application loop). harness-view gains only the hsk-studio-ui edge; winit and ash never enter its closure. kumihimo-core comes in as an exact vendored tree, see the pin position.
positions.why: Keeps Viewer's 80+ test binaries from rebuilding when window or Vulkan code changes, gives builders small crates with fast checks and few shared files, and leaves a clean lift. The CPU painter is the key parallelism move: panel builders and the designer see real pixels with no Vulkan, no window and no GPU lease, and STU-QUIET-005 asks for render-to-buffer proof; the Vulkan team and the panel teams stop blocking each other.

positions.blocker: Layout and docking: Layout Presets, Task Scope, Context Bar
positions.decision: Two layout levels. Regions and centre tree: kumihimo-core plans. Inside panels: Taffy flex and grid through its low-level API, using STU-SHL-072's numbers as theme tokens (row pitch 28, field 72x24, Inspect Dock 300 and 260). Layout Preset is a data file of dock arrangement, Tool Rail order and search bias, the only three things STU-SHL-093 lets it hold. Task Scope is a clause kind in the availability predicate, never a layout. Context Bar is a two-zone node at region top whose Tool Zone resolves from the active tool's descriptor set or the active Task Scope, and Selection Zone from the slot resolver.
positions.why: The spec already fixes the mechanisms and forbids merging preset and scope. Data-file presets let the GUI designer own arrangement with no code, and a proof that a preset gates nothing is two state-tree string reads. Taffy is what GPUI embeds.
positions.risk: STU-SHL-007 wants SurrealDB for durable layouts, and standalone Studio has none. The preset count is an open Operator item (STU-SHL-095).
positions.control: Layout persistence behind a port; standalone writes a JSON file through kumihimo-layout-json, marked asset-local, no other database. Ship presets as data so the count can change freely.
positions.proven_wrong_if: A dense panel cannot meet STU-SHL-072/073's compact form under Taffy without per-panel special cases.
positions.unblocks: Designer lanes, default layouts per profile (SPEC14 section 4.5), Task Scope lanes.

positions.blocker: Layer-based compositing (STU-SHL-130) as it reaches the GUI
positions.decision: Correct the framing: STU-SHL-130 decides the document model, not the UI compositor. For the GUI it means Layers panel and keyframe-timeline rows read the layer tree, comp-flowchart stays a read-only projection, and no node editor is built. Separately, the GUI's own frame is an ordered set of display-list layers: canvas image, canvas overlay (gizmos, marching ants, guides), dock chrome and panels, floating panels, popups and menus, tooltip, drag preview. Canvas image is a texture updated from Frame.rgba8. Layers repaint independently, so a canvas change does not rebuild panels. Swapchain is UNORM with sRGB nonlinear colour space, so sRGB-encoded frame bytes pass through unchanged; panels blend in gamma space.
positions.why: The clause text says it plainly. Treating it as UI compositing would mislead lanes. Field: GPUI's layers and stacking give z-order the same way. Frame already provides the read-back bytes with backend named.
positions.risk: Full-frame upload per edit on large documents. No display colour management yet, and proof preview tolerance depends on it.
positions.control: Dirty-rect upload as a later small change once render reports rects; display profile stays a named gap, and the view reports it in state.
positions.proven_wrong_if: Gamma-space panel blending is rejected by the designer on real shots; switch panels to a linear pass and keep the canvas exact.

positions.blocker: Text through hsk-studio-type plus an atlas
positions.decision: Use Type for shaping and raster, with a cache layer and one small Type addition. hsk-studio-ui-text reuses the Request and Ports plumbing already in view/text.rs and caches shaped lines by (text, font stack, size) and glyph coverage by (font hash, glyph id, px size, 1/4 px x-offset). Add a verified-font session to Type: hash once, then outlines and shaping skip re-hashing, same results. Atlas lives in the renderer: alpha-only page, own shelf allocator of about 100 lines, whole-page reset on full. Rejected etagere, since no per-glyph deallocation is needed and it is one more fetch. UI fonts: static Inter plus Noto SC fallback, already fixtures in the repo, moved to a resource with licence files. A coverage contrast LUT is a theme token. No stem darkening in v1.
positions.why: Brief and spec want the existing stack, and it has real shaping (complex scripts, bidi) that an egui-style stack lacked. But Type is built for documents: glyph_outlines and shaping hash full inputs per call with soft SHA-256, and each call carries about 20 request fields, so uncached use at UI rates is not viable (reading of code; UNVERIFIED by timing). GPUI's design shows the cache keys and alpha atlas work. FreeType's note says stem darkening without linear blending goes fuzzy, so do not enable it.
evidence: P hsk-studio-type/src/outline.rs:184-225; validate.rs:40-47,135; contract.rs Request; Cargo.toml sha2 force-soft; descriptor.rs:11 raster parity note
positions.risk: Top visual risk: unhinted greyscale is lighter at small sizes per Type's own descriptor, on a 96 dpi screen at 11-12 px, in a dense pro UI. Outlines refuse CFF2, colour and variable axes. No emoji.
positions.control: Designer judges real shots at 100%, 150%, 200% in the first text commit. Tune LUT and baseline pixel snap. If still rejected, add a raster-only hinter through a permissive crate behind the text port, without touching shaping. Refused fonts are typed outcomes with fallback to the bundled stack.
positions.proven_wrong_if: Designer rejects 11-12 px text at 96 dpi after LUT and snap; or the cache misses cost more than a frame in normal panel use.
positions.unblocks: Every panel; IME preedit display; the text tool's font default after RF-01.

positions.decision: Host maps winit events to a platform-free input stream into hsk-studio-ui; nothing else sees winit. Pointer: arbiter implements STU-SHL-101..108 claim-at-press, with an observable studio.gesture.active. winit's SetCapture on press gives tracking past the window; raw motion gives deltas. Never warp. Focus: one owner per window, tab order from tree order, explicit focus scopes per region. DPI: logical units in the tree, physical at paint, rebuild on scale change, atlas keyed by px size. IME: set_ime_allowed only while a text field holds focus, set_ime_cursor_area from the caret rect, preedit drawn by the field. AccessKit: accesskit_winit adapter fed from the semantic tree, node id hashed from author_id per STU-MDL-104, actions routed to the same dispatcher as model invoke. Semantic node takes the shape STU-MDL-105 gives: id, author_id, node_id, role, label, value, disabled, actions, bounds, children plus numeric and temporal fields, and availability fields of STU-MDL-107, which AccessKit cannot carry as custom properties and which therefore also ship in the state tree. Keep accesskit at the locked 0.21.1, with the Kumihimo accesskit_windows patch for non-activating roots.
positions.why: egui's scrub and gesture logic in egui_adapter.rs is the costliest part to lose; moving it to renderer-free code makes it testable. Winit docs give every IME and cursor call needed; ImGui's FAQ shows HWND-bound IME is a known hazard that winit handles. All required AccessKit setters exist at the locked version.
positions.risk: STU-SHL-104 asks for a hidden cursor at a screen edge with continued delta and restore at the press point, yet forbids warping, and restoring at the press point is itself a cursor move; set_cursor_visible hides only inside the window on Windows. IME behaviour needs a real Japanese or Chinese IME session. Physical assistive hardware unproven, as at Kumihimo.
positions.control: Host lane proves drag past edge with raw motion; if hiding outside the window fails, report the exact limit and keep delta accumulation. Scripted IME event tests plus one Operator manual check, listed in operator-items.
positions.proven_wrong_if: Raw motion stops at the screen edge during capture, or accesskit_winit cannot run with the renderer's windows hidden and non-activated.

positions.blocker: Model use: ids, state tree, process-level drive
positions.decision: Extend SMB-HARNESS-DRIVE-1's JSONL loop, with no second protocol. Add gui.tree (semantic tree JSON, explicit truncation per STU-MDL-108), gui.invoke {author_id, action, value} (the same dispatcher as AccessKit ActionRequest), gui.shot {out, scale, dpi} (CPU painter PNG; Vulkan offscreen with a flag), gui.resize, gui.input (synthetic stream into the UI layer, never the OS, for gesture tests), plus --actor and --session. No window opens for any of them. Observability nodes studio.dock.state, studio.slot.<slot>.resolved, studio.gesture.active appear in gui.tree. Parallel models run one process each with their own Viewer, so agent view, selection and navigation are isolated by construction; saves rest on SMB-SESSION-WRITE-SAFETY-1. Workflow scenarios in S/workflows run as these JSONL scripts. Manual gets the rows from the same table.
positions.why: STU-MDL-109 allows two paths, typed commands and the accessibility tree by author_id; gui.invoke is the second one with no platform in the way. STU-QUIET-001 and 002 require headless and no OS input. A separate process per model is the cheapest honest answer to STU-ARC-014 and GUI-DESKTOP-045, while Viewer has one selection field. It turns the workflow agents' scenarios into runnable GUI checks, as HANDOFF workflow item 14 wants.
positions.risk: No model path into a live operator window yet except UIA. One Viewer per process means a model and the operator on one file only meet at the session layer, and presence and pending proposals (14.21) are not covered. Tree JSON can be large.
positions.control: A later --control-pipe on the window host uses the same JSONL with a per-client view state; do not start it until scenarios need it. Bounded tree with a subtree query by author_id prefix.
positions.proven_wrong_if: A workflow scenario step can be done by pointer but not by gui.invoke, or a gui.* call opens a window or takes focus (negative test).
positions.unblocks: STU-CON-007 visual verifiability; designer and workflow agents; GUI-tests without pixel diffs.

positions.blocker: Order: spec chain versus 'show a panel now'
positions.decision: Follow STU-SHL-110 with two readings to record. SHL-P-01 and 02 are Handshake shell steps, not applicable to the standalone host, and stay owed at embedding. 'Passed acceptance' before fan-out means the seven STU-SHL-109 tests and the byte-identical reselect test are green at the lane tip, since rounds now run in batches; READY stays unjudged. The eight-panel spine ships first and includes Layers, so the first real panel is inside the law, not ahead of it. Fan-out lanes start only after this spine gate.
positions.why: STU-SHL-109 says the tests 'MUST exist and MUST pass before any further panel is authored', and the spec names SHL-P-03, 09 and 12 as where the risk sits. Skipping them to look fast means repairing 25 panels. It costs little: those tests are headless string reads in the new crate.
positions.risk: Colour and History panels do not exist in the Viewer, so the spine needs new logic. The gate holds up visible breadth, against the Operator's taste for width.
positions.control: Engine and width lanes keep running on Viewer methods and descriptors meanwhile, so no team idles; their view functions wait. History can read the chronicle's existing op list.
positions.proven_wrong_if: The gate blocks fan-out over more than the toolkit lanes' own commits with no failing test to show for it. Then open fan-out on hosted forms only.

Pixels through gui.shot once SMB-UI-TREE-1, SMB-UI-TEXT-1 and SMB-GUI-DRIVE-2 land; a real window once SMB-UI-VK-1 and SMB-GUI-HOST-1 land.
